claim: Laser-created plasma can function as a dynamically configurable radio antenna, with geometry and direction controlled by beam parameters rather than mechanical deployment.
verifiedFacts: NC State reported Oct. 5 a laser-induced plasma-filament antenna transmitting at 30 MHz VHF.
Length and direction can be changed via laser parameters and beam steering.
inference: Inferred: programmable field geometry is a design variable at the optics/EM/radio boundary.
Inferred: this is a high-signal experimental demonstration opportunity, not product evidence.
Unknown: scale, receiving capability and space qualification.
significance: Adds a concrete radio-physics thread and a bounded wave-field demonstration opportunity.
assumptions: Conceptual models must distinguish simulation from experimental validation.
knownLimitations: Power efficiency, range and receiving capability are missing.
